questions.title: Which senior Chinese official will hold talks with Jo Yong Won in Pyongyang in the first half of July 2026?
questions.background: Jo Yong Won is a senior official in North Korea's governing Workers' Party. Chinese President Xi Jinping visited North Korea in June 2026 as Beijing and Pyongyang sought closer ties.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : KCNA, as reported by Reuters, identifying the senior Chinese official holding talks with Jo Yong Won in Pyongyang between July 1 and July 15, 2026, inclusive. Resolution Date : 2026-07-16 Accepted Answer Format : string (name). Answer with the Chinese official's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Xi Jinping completed a high-profile state visit to Pyongyang on June 8-9, 2026 (joined by Cai Qi, Wang Yi, Dong Jun, Liu Haixing, and others), and July 11, 2026 marks the 65th anniversary of the 1961 China-North Korea Treaty of Friendship. Crucially, on June 22, 2026, North Korea moved Jo Yong Won from SPA Standing Committee Chairman to Head of the WPK Organization Guidance Department. His direct party counterparts are CCP International Department head Liu Haixing and CCP Organization Department head Shi Taifeng, while Politburo/PSC Pyongyang anniversary envoys Li Hongzhong (July 2023), Zhao Leji (April 2024), and Secretariat chief Cai Qi are also strong contenders; 41% remains on the wider Politburo/PSC field (Wang Huning, Liu Guozhong, Ding Xuexiang, He Lifeng, Li Shulei, etc.).

local_articles.title: N. Korea's premier to visit China to mark 65th anniv. of signing of friendship treaty: KCNA
local_articles.snippet: North Korean Premier Pak Thae-song will make an official visit to China to mark the 65th anniversary of the signing of a friendship treaty between the two nations, Pyongyang's state media said Thursday. A North Korean delegation, led by Pak, will travel to China to "take part in the event marking the 65th anniversary of the conclusion of the DPRK-China Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual assistance," at the invitation of China's Communist Party, the Korean Central News Agency said. DPRK stands for the North's official name, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. The two countries signed the treaty on July 11, 1961, by the North's state founder Kim Il-sung and then Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai.

questions.title: Which U.S. state will be the first to impose a statewide moratorium on construction of large new hyperscale data centres?
questions.background: Hyperscale data centres are large facilities designed to provide computing and storage capacity at massive scale. Their development can place substantial demands on electricity grids and water supplies.
questions.resolution_criteria: Qualifying Event : Resolve to the first U.S. state to formally impose, by December 31, 2026, a statewide temporary moratorium on construction or permitting of large new hyperscale data centres. Proposed legislation, vetoed measures, and restrictions limited to individual municipalities do not qualify. Source of Truth : Official state-government announcements, corroborated by reliable contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution occurs when the qualifying moratorium is publicly announced as imposed. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the state.
questions.current_reasoning: July 1-3 reporting (Cliff Daily, New Pine Plains Herald, Highlands Current) confirms New York's Responsible Data Center Development Act (S10642/A11560, passed Senate 44-16 and Assembly 102-39 on June 4) has still not been formally delivered to Gov. Kathy Hochul, which policy analysts read as active chapter-amendment negotiations signaling Hochul is likely to sign a narrowed version (higher MW threshold/in-progress carve-outs, still qualifying as a statewide moratorium on large new hyperscale data centers) rather than issue an outright veto. Progressive NY primary victories and early-July heatwave power-conservation alerts further raise election-year pressure on Hochul ahead of November, while no competing state passed a statewide construction moratorium through July 6 (VA/FL/IL July 1 measures were tax/tariff/incentive policies; MN and MI actions remain municipal only; Maine's bill was already vetoed with override failed). Raising New York from 0.74 to 0.79 (retaining ~21% veto/collapse/other-state risk) and reallocating secondary slots to active full-time legislatures (Michigan 0.04, Pennsylvania 0.03, California 0.03, New Jersey 0.02; 9% residual).

local_articles.title: Tadej Pogacar demolishes rivals on the Tourmalet to take ominous Tour de France lead
local_articles.snippet: dej Pogacar powered alone to the summit of the mighty Col du Tourmalet, deep in the Hautes-Pyrénées, and rode on to victory on stage six to Gavarnie-Gèdre, taking an emphatic overall lead in the 2026 Tour de France. In the shadow of the towering cliffs of the Cirque de Gavarnie, and under the gaze of French president Emmanuel Macron, Pogacar was imperious. Only his perennial rival, Jonas Vingegaard, was able to give chase and by the end of the stage, even his resistance seemed futile. All the labels that have been applied to Pogacar – ogre, monster, beast – were appropriate as he embarked on another of his trademark solo raids, crushing the morale of his opponents yet again. local_articles.title: Traeen pulls out of Tour de France following crash on mountain stage
local_articles.snippet: July 9 - Norway's Torstein Traeen is out of the Tour de France after suffering a concussion and multiple rib fractures in a crash on Thursday's seventh stage, his Uno-X Mobility team said. The rider crashed on the descent of the Col du Tourmalet during the race's first major mountain test, colliding with the back of teammate Anders Halland Johannessen's bike. The 30-year-old Traeen was assessed by race medical staff in an ambulance before continuing and finishing the stage. The withdrawal cut short a historic run for Traeen and his Norwegian team. He claimed the overall leader's yellow jersey after the fourth stage and successfully defended it through the fifth stage, securing the first-ever days in yellow for the Uno-X Mobility team before losing the overall race lead to Tadej Pogacar during a punishing alpine stage won by the Slovenian. local_articles.title: Apple set to overtake Google as world's second-most valuable company: What's driving the surge?
local_articles.snippet: Apple is very close to becoming the world's second-most valuable company, behind Nvidia. This means Apple is likely to move ahead of Alphabet if its stock continues to perform well.
